title: DuckStation protects Warcraft II video timing from CD-ROM acceleration
summary: A per-title MDEC trait keeps accelerated reads from speeding up full-motion video while leaving the user's broader disc-speed setting available outside those sequences.
heroAlt: Source evidence from DuckStation pull request #3600: GameDB: Disable disc speedup on MDEC for Warcraft II

sourceLabels.duckstation-pr-3600: GameDB: Disable disc speedup on MDEC for Warcraft II

blocks.text: Disc acceleration can leak into a movie's playback clock

DuckStation's CD-ROM Read Speedup reduces waiting in games that tolerate faster delivery. Warcraft II's full-motion video path does not treat those reads as an independent loading optimization: feeding MDEC data faster changes how the sequence plays. The resulting issue is not a decoding error in individual frames but incorrect presentation speed caused by a timing option that remains active during streamed video.
DisableCDROMSpeedupOnMDEC narrows the exception to movie decoding

Pull request #3600 adds an existing GameDB trait to Warcraft II. When MDEC video is active, DuckStation stops applying the accelerated read behavior; outside that path, the user's speedup setting can continue. This is more precise than disabling CD-ROM acceleration for the entire title and safer than changing MDEC timing globally for games that already work with speedup enabled.
The trait is applied to all three known regional serials

SLES-00878, SLPS-01098, and SLUS-00480 receive the same compatibility entry. Covering Europe, Japan, and North America avoids a region-dependent experience for a problem rooted in the shared game engine. Keeping the serial list explicit also leaves room for a variant with different streaming behavior to be tested rather than automatically inheriting an assumption.
FMV duration and post-movie loading both need measurement

Enable CD-ROM speedup and time the same Warcraft II movie against speedup disabled, checking audio synchronization, frame pacing, and total duration. Repeat for every listed region and several cutscenes. After the movie ends, confirm speedup resumes for normal loading and that skipping a movie does not leave the trait latched. Other MDEC-heavy games should serve as negative controls so the GameDB exception remains isolated to Warcraft II.
The compatibility rule pauses one optimization during MDEC playback; it does not penalize every Warcraft II disc read.
